settings.subtitle: Michelin is the brand most Calgary drivers ask for by name. We stock the CrossClimate2 (all-weather), X-Ice Snow (winter), Defender 2 (all-season), and Pilot Sport A/S 4 (performance) — installed same day at 111 42 Ave SW with price-match guarantee.
settings.intro_heading: Why we recommend Michelin in Calgary
settings.intro_richtext:
Michelin is the tire most Calgary drivers ask for by name — and the one we recommend most often when the priority is safety, longevity, and predictable behaviour through Alberta's freeze-thaw chinooks.

The CrossClimate2 is our top seller. It carries the 3PMSF (three-peak mountain snowflake) certification required by Alberta and BC winter-tire laws, so you don't have to swap twice a year if you don't want to. It performs in -25°C, wet spring potholes on 16th Ave, and 30°C summer pavement on the Stoney Trail ring road.

For drivers who still prefer a dedicated winter tire — and for anyone running highway trips into Banff or BC on Highway 93 — the X-Ice Snow is the answer. It stays flexible below -20°C, where cheaper compounds go glassy and stop gripping on packed snow.

Every Michelin we install gets the same balance, calibrated torque, and TPMS reset as a premium-priced job — and we price-match any local Calgary competitor on the same model. Book your installation or call (403) 452-4283.
settings.faq_1_q: What's the best Michelin tire for Calgary winters?
settings.faq_1_a: For most Calgary drivers, the CrossClimate2 (3PMSF-rated all-weather) is the right pick — you keep it on year-round and skip the seasonal swap. If you want a dedicated winter tire for the worst conditions, the X-Ice Snow is Michelin's flagship winter and our most-installed winter tire from October through April.
settings.faq_2_q: How much do Michelin tires cost in Calgary?
settings.faq_2_a: Michelin tires at Prince Tires range from about $220 to $490 per tire depending on size and model. The CrossClimate2 starts around $260 in common 17" sizes; the Defender 2 starts around $230. Installation, balancing, and TPMS reset are billed separately. We price-match any written quote from another Calgary tire shop on the same model.
settings.faq_3_q: Can I get same-day Michelin installation in Calgary?
settings.faq_3_a: Yes for most common sizes if you book before midday. We stock the CrossClimate2, X-Ice Snow, Defender 2, and Pilot Sport A/S 4 in the most common Calgary fitments. Trucks and bigger vehicles need a 60-minute slot — call (403) 452-4283 to confirm a bay is free.
settings.faq_4_a: Michelin's standard treadwear warranty ranges from 96,000 km on the Pilot Sport A/S 4 up to 130,000 km on the Defender 2 — the longest-wearing all-season touring tire we carry. The CrossClimate2 carries a 96,000 km warranty. All Michelin tires include Michelin's standard road-hazard and manufacturer defect coverage.
settings.faq_5_q: Where can I buy Michelin tires near downtown Calgary?
settings.faq_5_a: Prince Tires is at 111 42 Ave SW — five minutes south of downtown off Macleod Trail, easy access from Deerfoot. We're open Monday to Saturday 9:30am to 5:30pm and Sundays 10:00am to 3:30pm.
settings.faq_6_q: Do you install Michelin tires I bought somewhere else?
settings.faq_6_a: Yes. We install customer-supplied tires — Michelin or any brand. Standard installation is $50–60 per tire and includes mounting, balancing, valve stem service, and TPMS reset on standard sizes. Bring the tires in or have them shipped to our shop at 111 42 Ave SW Calgary.
settings.cta_description: Most common Michelin sizes in stock. Same-day install on confirmed bookings — price-matched against any local Calgary competitor.
settings.calgary_richtext: Calgary drivers see Michelin most often in our winter and all-weather lanes. X-Ice Snow handles the deep-freeze mornings on Deerfoot Trail — it stays flexible at -30°C when cheaper rubber goes glassy. CrossClimate2 is what we install for anyone tired of swapping twice a year; it carries the 3PMSF mark and meets Alberta's winter-tire law. Pilot Sport 4 sees a lot of city use on performance sedans and EVs. Premium price, but tread life on Calgary's rough winter potholes consistently outlasts the warranty.
settings.awards_text: Consumer Reports Best Tire Brand 2024; J.D. Power Highest Rated for Tread Wear in multiple categories.
settings.testimonial_quote: Switched to Michelin X-Ice Snow on my Outback last fall — gripped at -32°C on Stoney Trail when my old tires would have spun. Worth every dollar.
